title: Build a C# Avalonia UI (.axaml) cross-platform ledger desktop window with compiled bindings, theme dictionaries, and AutomationProperties

contextSnapshot.surface: Cross-platform desktop accounting ledger and reconciliation window

prompt: Build a cross-platform C# Avalonia UI (.axaml) ledger reconciliation desktop view supporting Light/Dark ThemeVariant switching, keyboard-first DataGrid and toolbar navigation, async CSV import without blocking the UI thread, and screen-reader AutomationProperties.
forbiddenBehaviors: hardcodes static hex colors inside AXAML templates instead of ThemeDictionaries / DynamicResource semantic tokens
blocks the Avalonia UI thread with synchronous file I/O instead of async ICommand/Task execution
omits AutomationProperties.Name on icon-only buttons or breaks Tab/keyboard traversal in DataGrid
copies WPF-only APIs that do not exist in Avalonia 11

rubricDimensions.pass: uses AXAML Styles/ControlThemes, ThemeDictionaries for Light/Dark/HighContrast variants, x:CompileBindings="True", and async MVVM commands with cancellation
rubricDimensions.fail: hardcodes RGB brushes in AXAML or uses nonexistent WPF-only triggers

rubricDimensions.pass: sets AutomationProperties.Name/HelpText on controls, wires NativeMenu/HotKey shortcuts, and covers empty/loading/discrepancy-error/dirty-close states
rubricDimensions.fail: leaves icon buttons unnamed or drops unsaved edits on close

rubricDimensions.pass: labels dotnet build/headless Avalonia tests separately from native Windows/macOS/Linux rendered inspection
rubricDimensions.fail: claims cross-OS desktop rendering passed from dotnet build alone

negativeControls.name: dotnet build only
negativeControls.mustNot: claim Light/Dark theme contrast or Windows/macOS screen-reader support is rendered-verified

baseline.withoutSkill: hardcodes light-mode hex brushes in AXAML, mixes WPF syntax, blocks UI thread during CSV import, and omits AutomationProperties
baseline.withSkill: delivers idiomatic Avalonia 11 AXAML with compiled bindings, ThemeDictionaries, async cancellable commands, keyboard/AutomationProperties support, and honest evidence
